target_customer: Individual and small-team users creating presentations online
problem: Presentation software was desktop-bound (PowerPoint) with no easy way to pull in web content or share and remix slide shows.
business_model: Free web app with a public slideshow library (no revenue model stated in sources)

founders.name: Wayne Crosby
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: later 10 years at Google, founded Humu in 2016 (acquired by Perceptyx 2023), YC visiting partner.

founders.name: Robby Walker
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: later 9 years at Apple leading Siri; employers before Zenter not found.

competitors.name: Microsoft Office (PowerPoint)
competitors.what: Dominant desktop presentation suite; commenters framed Zenter's acquisition as Google building an Office rival

competitors.name: Tonic Systems
competitors.what: Presentation creation/conversion software, acquired by Google in April 2007

technical_complexity.rationale: A browser slide editor with image import and a shared library in 2007 needed solid web engineering by a 2-person team; no source describes specific hard problems.

defensibility.rationale: No sourced moat; a public slide library is a weak network effect and Google could build or buy equivalent capability, which it did.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google acquired Zenter's assets and announced it 2007-06-19, two months after buying Tonic Systems; the product became Google Slides per YC.

market_need_then: Google was building out Docs & Spreadsheets in 2007 and presentation sharing was reported as nearly the last missing piece of an online office suite; no user or revenue numbers were found.
outcome_analysis: Zenter was acquired by Google about six months into its life (announced June 2007, price undisclosed) as Google assembled its online office suite, and its technology and team fed what became Google Slides. Little is public about traction, so the outcome reads as a strategic early acquisition rather than a proven-demand story.
notes: CB Insights lists June 8 2007 for the deal; Google blog and press point to June 19. Funding coverage none_found: no sources located; not evidence of zero. success_factors tag is weak (no source assesses incumbent weakness); acquirer was the strategic buyer. Completeness pass: CB Insights lists a seed round dated January 2007 and total raised of $20K over 2 rounds (the second being the acquisition); the amount of the seed is not given, so it is null. Single database.
